verdict.summary: Self-serve: you create the Xero app yourself and it works at once for 5 customer organisations, or 50 once you add a credit card. No review is found up to 50. Beyond 50 you need Xero certification, which takes months and has no official timeline. Each customer's own Xero organisation also allows only five uncertified apps.

calendar.label: Same day to start (up to 50 connections); months more if you need over 50, with no official wait

questions.text: How many customer Xero organisations will connect through your app?
Do your customers' Xero organisations already connect many other third-party apps?

variants.summary: Past 50 connections you must get your app certified by Xero (the Plus tier allows 1,000 connections). You need 10 active customer connections, a Sign Up with Xero flow and an application through Manage Plan. A security self-assessment is needed before 1,000 connections.
variants.calendar_label: Several months; Xero states no overall wait
notes: Certification means building to Xero's eight checkpoints: roughly 40 to 120 hours of engineering (our estimate, not Xero's).
The Plus tier costs AUD 245 a month; there is no separate certification fee in the pages we read.
Certified apps are not subject to the per-organisation five-app limit.

variants.summary: Your app works, but a customer whose Xero organisation already has five uncertified apps cannot add yours until they remove one or your app is certified.
variants.calendar_label: Same day for you; depends on each customer's organisation
notes: The five-app limit counts uncertified apps in the customer's organisation, not your connection count.
A Custom Connection (one organisation, extra monthly subscription) is not counted toward the five-app limit.

variants.summary: Add a credit card in the developer portal to move from Starter (5 connections) to Core (50 connections, AUD 35 a month). We found no review step for this.
notes: Docs say a card moves you to Core, but the Manage Plan screen was not seen; check it on first sign-in.

variants.summary: A new app starts on the free Starter tier with 5 connections and no card. It works as soon as you create it.
notes: Starter allows 1,000 API calls a day per organisation.
You can test on the Xero demo company.

byo_advice: Composio has no managed Xero app, so you bring your own: create the Xero app, then give Composio its client ID and secret. Use your own product name on it. Check Xero's developer terms before you serve many customers from one app (see open questions).

steps.title: Sign in to the Xero developer portal (or sign up)
steps.detail: Open https://developer.xero.com/app/manage. You are sent to the Xero login. Create a free Xero account first if you have none.

evidence.label: TESTED
evidence.note: developer.xero.com/app/manage redirected to login.xero.com/identity/user/login on 2026-10-21; the page showed Email and Password fields and a Sign up link, with no bot check.

steps.title: Enable the Xero demo company
steps.detail: In your Xero account (My Xero) turn on the demo company. You will use it to test the connection without touching a real customer's books.

evidence.label: DOCS
evidence.quote: Enable the Xero demo company

steps.title: Create the app: My Apps > New app, integration type Auth Code
steps.detail: Give it your product name (the name cannot include the word Xero), choose the standard Auth Code (web server) type, and enter your company or application URL. Accept Xero's developer terms and create it. Do not choose PKCE or Custom connection: PKCE apps get no client secret, and a Custom Connection serves only one organisation.

values.label: App name
values.value: <Your product name, without the word Xero>

evidence.label: DOCS
evidence.quote: create an OAuth2 app and make sure you select the “Auth Code” grant type
evidence.note: Quote covers the Auth Code grant type. The New app button wording appears only in the Custom Connections section of the docs; the form fields and terms checkbox were seen only in an older-looking docs image. None of it was seen in a signed-in run.

steps.title: Add Composio's callback as the redirect URI
steps.detail: Paste the redirect URI from your Composio auth config. It must be https. http://localhost is allowed for testing but http://127.0.0.1 is not, and wildcards are not supported.

evidence.label: DOCS
evidence.quote: This must be an https address, however for testing you can use http://localhost/
evidence.note: Where the redirect URI field sits in the portal was not seen; the docs do not say.

steps.title: Generate a client secret
steps.detail: On the app's configuration page, generate a client secret. Copy it somewhere safe; treat it as private.

evidence.label: DOCS
evidence.quote: Your app is assigned a unique Client ID and you can then generate a Client Secret
evidence.note: The real Generate secret button was not seen without signing in.

steps.title: Request offline_access and the minimum granular scopes
steps.detail: Scopes are requested in the authorization request, so set them in your Composio auth config rather than in the Xero form. Include offline_access (without it you get no refresh token) and the openid scopes, plus only the granular accounting scopes you need. New apps use granular scopes instead of the broad accounting.transactions scope.

values.label: Scopes
values.value: openid profile email offline_access accounting.invoices.read accounting.contacts.read accounting.settings.read

evidence.label: DOCS
evidence.quote: To get a refresh token, you must request the offline_access scope.
evidence.note: Where Composio exposes the scope setting was not checked here. Scope names come from Xero's scopes page; see prepared scopes.

steps.title: Add the client ID and secret to a Composio auth config
steps.detail: Create a Composio auth config for Xero with your own app's client ID and secret, then confirm the redirect URI it shows matches step 4.

evidence.label: DOCS
evidence.quote: set its authorized redirect URI to Composio's callback, then pass the client ID and secret

steps.title: Connect the demo company and test the flow
steps.detail: Run the Composio connect flow with a Xero login that can access the demo company. Connect the demo organisation and make a test call.

steps.detail: Once you are on Core, open the Developer Centre, select your app and click Manage Plan to complete the application. Xero checks prerequisites such as a Sign Up with Xero flow and ten active customer connections, then reviews against its certification checkpoints. A security self-assessment is needed before 1,000 connections.

evidence.note: The application form itself was not seen.

steps.detail: Xero states no overall wait for certification. The security assessment, when required, is annual.

evidence.label: DOCS

review.trigger: More than 50 customer connections (the Plus tier requires App Certification), an App Store listing, or premium features such as the Journals endpoint and Practice Manager APIs. Practice APIs and financial services apps need Xero's prior approval before you can apply.
submit: Application through Manage Plan in the Xero Developer Centre (after reaching the Core plan)
A Sign Up with Xero flow and ten active customer connections
An integration that meets Xero's certification checkpoints, including minimal scopes with an explanation and the offline_access scope
A test account for Xero, if they ask for one
A security self-assessment, annually, before 1,000 connections or when using Practice Manager APIs
review.reviewer: Xero, against its certification checkpoints; Xero's security team reviews the security self-assessment.
review.wait_official: Security assessment only: about 5 working days for you to complete, then 5 to 10 working days for Xero to assess your answers (text from the 2020 rollout). No wait is stated for certification or the Plus tier.
review.wait_community: Several months to become a Xero App Partner (Codat, undated vendor documentation); anecdotal.
review.cost: No separate certification fee found. Tier fees apply: Core AUD 35 a month, Plus AUD 245 a month, plus egress overage.

gotchas.text: Request granular scopes on a new app. Apps created on or after 2 March 2026 already use them, and accounting.transactions is replaced by accounting.invoices, accounting.payments, accounting.banktransactions and accounting.manualjournals. Check the scopes in your Composio auth config.

evidence.label: DOCS
evidence.quote: Apps created on or after 2 March 2026 already use granular scopes. Existing apps have until 13 September 2027 to migrate.

gotchas.text: Unused refresh tokens expire after 60 days, after which the user must re-authorize.

evidence.label: DOCS
evidence.quote: Unused refresh tokens expire after 60 days.

gotchas.text: Refresh tokens rotate: replace the old one with the new one returned. If the response is lost you can retry the old token for 30 minutes.

evidence.label: DOCS
evidence.quote: you can retry refreshing your existing refresh token for a grace period of 30 minutes

gotchas.text: A connection is one organisation. Several users connecting the same organisation count once toward your limit.

evidence.label: DOCS
evidence.quote: only one of those connections will count towards your connection limit

gotchas.text: Connections stay capped at your tier's maximum until you meet that tier's requirements.

evidence.label: DOCS
evidence.quote: Your connections are capped at the tier maximums until you meet that tier's requirements.

gotchas.text: Xero's developer terms forbid aggregating user data and supplying it to another app or third party. This may matter for a shared, multi-customer app; no Xero text we read addresses connector or agent platforms.

evidence.label: DOCS

gotchas.text: Under the same terms you are responsible for having your app's use cases approved by Xero.

blockers.symptom: A customer cannot add your app to their Xero organisation.
blockers.cause: Their organisation already has five uncertified apps connected.
blockers.fix: Ask them to disconnect an unused uncertified app, or get your app certified. A single-organisation customer could use a Custom Connection instead.

evidence.label: DOCS
evidence.quote: each organisation or practice is limited to connecting a maximum of five uncertified apps
evidence.note: Xero's exact error wording for this case was not seen.

blockers.symptom: Your sixth customer organisation cannot connect.
blockers.cause: The app is on the Starter tier, which allows 5 connections.
blockers.fix: Add payment details in the developer portal to move to Core (50 connections).

evidence.label: DOCS
evidence.quote: In order to add a 6th connection, you will need to first add your payment details.

blockers.symptom: Connections stop working after a long idle period, and users have to reconnect.
blockers.cause: Refresh tokens that go unused for 60 days expire.
blockers.fix: Refresh tokens regularly (Composio refreshes tokens for you) and ask the user to reconnect if the token has already expired.

evidence.label: DOCS
evidence.quote: Unused refresh tokens expire after 60 days.

blockers.symptom: Authorization or API calls fail when you request the broad accounting.transactions scope on a new app.
blockers.cause: New apps use granular scopes, and the broad accounting.transactions scope is replaced.
blockers.fix: Request accounting.invoices, accounting.payments, accounting.banktransactions or accounting.manualjournals instead.

evidence.label: DOCS
evidence.quote: Apps created on or after 2 March 2026 already use granular scopes. Existing apps have until 13 September 2027 to migrate.
evidence.note: The failure mode and exact Xero error were not observed; the docs only say new apps use granular scopes.

blockers.symptom: The connect flow fails with a redirect URI mismatch error.
blockers.cause: The redirect URI in the Xero app doesn't exactly match the one in your Composio auth config.
blockers.fix: Copy the redirect URI from the Composio auth config into the Xero app, character for character.

evidence.label: UNCERTAIN
evidence.note: Exact Xero error wording not verified in this run.

blockers.symptom: Your app stops growing at 999 connections.
blockers.cause: Until the security self-assessment is passed, connection numbers are capped at 999.
blockers.fix: Complete the security self-assessment that Xero shares at 800 connections.

evidence.label: DOCS
evidence.quote: your connection numbers will be capped at 999

open_questions: Does Xero allow one shared app (or Composio's multi-customer model) given the clause on aggregating and supplying user data? No Xero text addresses agent or connector platforms; ask Xero developer support before committing.
Would a separate Xero app per customer avoid a shared cap but conflict with the 'multiple versions of your app' clause? Not verified.
Uncertified apps per customer organisation: 2 or 5? We treat 5 as current (see conflicts).
Does Core really need no review? Docs say a card is enough; check Manage Plan on first sign-in.
Is Sign Up with Xero required for certification? One page lists it as a prerequisite; others differ.
Where the redirect URI field, secret button and Manage Plan screen sit in the live portal (needs a signed-in check).
Exact wording of Xero's redirect mismatch error and the error a customer sees at the five-app limit.
Overall certification wait: no official figure; only a vendor's 'several months'.
